_comment: Digests of the COMMITTED C tables, recorded here so the Rust build can
compare the two generations without a C parser. A reader should treat
ANY disagreement between this block and `output` as a byte-splice: the
interned pool is UNSEPARATED, so a stale offset table against a fresh
blob returns neighbouring entries spliced together, not an error.
RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 at HEAD 5ce311e6 AFTER the layer-3 regen that
closed the 160-byte skew. This block now describes the SAME generation as
`output` above, so the two agree: 6032 interned strings / 6033 offsets,
726671 string-table bytes / 98782 bytecode bytes, whole-table FNV-1a
3985478542. The skew this block used to record (726831 / 98737 / FNV
876896371, 5533 of 6032 digests mismatched) is GONE, not merely
re-described.
PRESERVED, NOT REBUILT: cards/build_lib.py carries this key forward
instead of deleting it on a rebuild, because no writer of `output` owns
it. Preserving the RECORD cannot tell whether it is still TRUE, so the
consumer fails loudly instead: engine_c_wip/tests/test_artifacts_consistent.c
section 6 compares every field below against the values compiled into
gen_data.c AND against cards/build/abilities_strings.bin. An absent block,
a stale block and a disagreeing block are all FAILs there -- never
'cannot cross-check', never 'agrees'.
⚠ ANY REGENERATION INVALIDATES THIS BLOCK. After running
bash engine_c_wip/tools/regen_all.sh the C artefacts change, this block
does not, and section 6 of that suite will FAIL until these numbers are
re-measured and updated. That failure is the intended tripwire.
